turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Please, ma'am, I'd rather not disturb her, I don't know her, and I don't want to make things awkward, if you don't mind my saying so.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be ignored, boy. You will call Estella, and you will play with her, as I have commanded.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I must insist that I'm not at all comfortable playing with your adopted daughter, and I really don't think it would be suitable for me, especially if it's against my sister's wishes.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my commands, boy? I will not be disobeyed, and you will play with Estella, or face my wrath.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I'm not sure I understand what you mean by 'play' with Miss Estella, and I'd rather not do anything that might cause any trouble or upset anyone, if you could please explain further.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, boy, because I have decreed it, and because it is good for her. I have seen to her education, and now I have seen to her recreation, and you will be the one to provide it. Do not make me repeat myself.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know if I'm quite the right person to provide any sort of recreation for Miss Estella, especially if it's something that you've already arranged for her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, boy, and you will play with Estella, for your own sake as well as hers. It is not for you to question my arrangements, but to follow my instructions.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know if my family can afford to have me take time away from my work, even for a little while. My father and sister are counting on me to help with the business, and I don't want to cause them any trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, boy, or I will be forced to make it clear to your family that their meager efforts are not worthy of my consideration.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I wouldn't want to trouble you, ma'am, but I'm not sure I'm the right person to play with Miss Estella. I'm afraid I might not be able to do her justice, and I wouldn't want to disappoint you or Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, boy, and that is to play with Estella, for it is a privilege for you to be in her presence, and to refuse would be an insult to both of us.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I'm not sure I understand what you mean by playing with Miss Estella. I don't want to cause any trouble, but I'm not familiar with what that would entail.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be questioned, boy. You will play the game I set out for you to play, and you will do it with all the enthusiasm and skill that I demand.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't have any games or toys to play with, and I'm not sure I could afford to lose anything if we were to play a game that involved things of value. I'm just a poor boy, and I don't want to risk losing something that might be important to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are no match for Estella, I dare say, and yet I shall indulge you. Bring her to me, that we may begin this game, and that you may learn what it means to play with one such as she.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know if I should fetch Miss Estella at this moment, as I'm not sure I can play with her in the way you've described. I'm just a simple boy from the village, and I don't want to do anything that might be improper.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do you think you can understand the complexities of our game? I will not be deterred by your lack of sophistication or your feeble excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I'm not sure I'd be a good teacher for Miss Estella, as I don't know much about the game you want us to play, and I wouldn't want to confuse her or make things awkward for her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I instruct, Pip, and fetch Estella at once. I will not be kept waiting by your vacillations.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
